title: Justice and Faith -- Ch. 8: Be Not Afraid
keywords: The Filipino Laity: Called to Be Holy
Second Plenary Council of the Philippines

primary_topics: Chapter 8 of 'Justice and Faith' -- CJP's BLD reflection on the Sunday-after-Feb-5-1995 gospel (Luke 5: Peter lowering the nets), structured around three exhortations of 'Be not afraid': to be holy, to go into mission, and of failure

Pope John Paul II's 'Be not afraid' as the theme of the Petrine ministry -- anchored in 'Crossing the Threshold of Hope' (1994) on redemption as the antidote to fear, and CJP's lay-Catholic application of it to the BLD community

The universal call to holiness as the first direction -- 1987 Synod of Bishops, Vatican II, and Bishop Teodoro Bacani's 'The Filipino Laity: Called to Be Holy' (1988) -- holiness defined as 'intimate union with God by loving Him above all things and by loving our fellowmen as ourselves'

The mission imperative (second direction) -- JPII's 'As the Father has sent me, so I send you'; PCP II 1991 New Evangelization message; BLD's 1994 mission statement (restoring Filipino family, BECs, strengthening parish, breaking yokes, raising prayer warriors)

The fearless-of-failure stance (third direction) -- Covenant House P60 million plan as the test case of corporate faith funding; 'If You say so, Lord, we will have the victory' as the closing refrain echoing Peter's words
sub_topics: Opening gospel -- Luke 5: Jesus preaches from Peter's empty boat; instructs Peter to lower the nets in daylight; Peter, weary but obedient ('if you say so, I will lower the nets'), obeys and catches so many fish 'their two boats were filled to almost sinking capacity'

Faith-and-obedience teaching -- Fr. Francis Fernandez (On Conversation with God Vol. 3, p. 235): without obedience everything is useless in God's eyes; St. Chrysostom: 'God does not need our work. He needs our obedience'

Filipino-English-translation joke -- politician-actor exhorts crowd 'Do not afraid. Strengthen your inside. For in the long of time, we will success!' -- used to soften the gravity of the 'banish all fear' message
'Be not afraid' as a biblical refrain -- Lk 1:30 (Mary), Mt 1:20 (Joseph), and Christ's repeated reassurances to fearful disciples

Crossing the Threshold of Hope (p. 219) quotation -- 'Have no fear of that which you yourselves have created...the power of Christ's Cross and Resurrection is greater than any evil which man could or should fear'

Direction 1 (do not be afraid to be holy) -- Mt 5:48 ('Be perfect, just as Your heavenly Father is perfect'); BLD's first-and-foremost community value; Bishop Bacani's definition of holiness as love (not piety alone)
Holiness as fulfilling ordinary tasks -- 'we grow in holiness through the loving performance of our ordinary tasks and obligations...'
Mother Teresa quotation when called a living saint -- 'What is so extraordinary about that? Are we not all called to holiness?'
Lorenzo Ruiz as the first Filipino Catholic saint and a lay person

Mercedes-Benz/jeep/bicycle wives joke -- three husbands at the pearly gates (teacher / lawyer / politician) receive vehicles by holiness; the politician's bicycle is funniest because his Mercedes-riding teacher friend later sobs after seeing his wife on a bicycle

Direction 2 (do not be afraid to go into mission) -- JPII's 'As the Father has sent me, so I send you'; Asia's 2.5 billion non-Catholics; Bill Clinton on Asia-Pacific economic growth vs JPII on the Holy Spirit's coming work in the region; PCP II's New Evangelization thrust

BLD 1994 mission statement (verbatim) -- five elements (restoring the Filipino family in Christ; forming BECs; strengthening the Filipino parish; breaking yokes of poverty and oppression; raising an army of prayer warriors)

Direction 3 (do not be afraid of failure) -- Covenant House P60 million plan, discerned since 1988, confirmed in BLD's discernment sessions; 'The Lord does not directly hand out money or land. He uses His faithful ones as His instruments'

Closing refrain -- 'If you say so, Lord, we will lower the nets. If You say so, Lord, we will build Your Covenant House. If You say so, Lord, we will not fear. If You say so, Lord, we will have victory'

one_paragraph_summary: Chapter 8 of 'Justice and Faith' is CJP's BLD prayer-meeting reflection on the Sunday-after-February-5,-1995 gospel -- Luke 5, in which Peter, weary after an all-night fruitless catch, obeys Jesus's instruction to lower his nets in daylight ('if you say so, I will lower the nets') and the two boats fill to sinking capacity. CJP turns Peter's obedience into the paradigm of faith ('without obedience, everything is useless in God's eyes' -- Chrysostom via Fernandez), then leavens the gravity with a Filipino-English-translation joke. He then unfolds three directions for 'Be not afraid,' the theme JPII chose for the Petrine ministry and anchored in 'Crossing the Threshold of Hope' (1994). First, 'do not be afraid to be holy' -- the universal call to holiness from the 1987 Synod of Bishops, Vatican II, and Bishop Teodoro Bacani's 'The Filipino Laity: Called to Be Holy' (1988); holiness defined not by piety but by 'loving accomplishment of whatever it is God wills for me here and now'; Mother Teresa ('Are we not all called to holiness?') and San Lorenzo Ruiz (the first Filipino Catholic saint, a layman) are the anchors, with a Mercedes/jeep/bicycle wives joke as the comedic illustration. Second, 'do not be afraid to go into mission' -- JPII's 'As the Father has sent me, so I send you'; the Pope looks to 55 million Filipino Catholics to lead Asia's New Evangelization to its 2.5 billion non-Catholics, echoing PCP II (1991)'s thrust under Archbishop Legaspi; the BLD's 1994 mission statement (restoring the Filipino family, forming BECs, strengthening the parish, breaking the yokes of poverty and oppression, raising prayer warriors) is the concrete response. Third, 'do not be afraid of failure' -- the Covenant House P60 million plan, discerned since 1988 and confirmed in BLD discernment sessions, becomes the corporate test: 'The Lord does not directly hand out money or land. He uses His faithful ones as His instruments.' He closes with a fourfold refrain echoing Peter -- 'If you say so, Lord, we will lower the nets. If You say so, Lord, we will build Your Covenant House. If You say so, Lord, we will not fear. If You say so, Lord, we will have victory.'
